source_refs.note: Exercise 14.3, Question 2 (i)-(iv): unit vector perpendicular to the plane of a and b, and sin of the angle, via a x b (book p.282). Answer key PDF 312 (gives the + unit vector only).

blocks.prompt: 2 (i) Find a unit vector perpendicular to the plane containing \(\underline{a}\) and \(\underline{b}\). Also find sine of the angle between them: \(\underline{a} = \underline{i} + 6\underline{j} - 3\underline{k}\), \(\underline{b} = 2\underline{i} + \underline{j} + 3\underline{k}\).
blocks.explanation:
Is sawal mein do cheezein chahiye: ek unit vector jo dono vectors par perpendicular ho, aur un ke darmiyan angle ka sine.
Achhi baat yeh hai ke dono ek hi cross product se nikal aati hain.
Plan: \(\underline{a} \times \underline{b}\) nikalein, us ki lambai se divide karein; phir \(\sin\theta = |\underline{a} \times \underline{b}|/(|\underline{a}||\underline{b}|)\).
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(\underline{a} = \underline{i} + 6\underline{j} - 3\underline{k}\), \(\underline{b} = 2\underline{i} + \underline{j} + 3\underline{k}\).
Humein find karna hai: aisa unit vector (lambai 1 wala vector) jo \(\underline{a}\) aur \(\underline{b}\) wale plane par perpendicular ho, aur dono ke darmiyan angle ka \(\sin\theta\).
Tareeqa: \(\underline{a} \times \underline{b}\) hamesha dono vectors par perpendicular hota hai, is liye un ke plane par bhi. Is vector ko us ki apni lambai se divide karein to lambai 1 reh jati hai, yani unit vector mil jata hai. Phir definition \(|\underline{a} \times \underline{b}| = |\underline{a}||\underline{b}|\sin\theta\) se \(\sin\theta\) nikal aata hai. Ek hi cross product se dono jawab!

Determinant likhein
\[\underline{a} \times \underline{b} = \begin{vmatrix} \underline{i} & \underline{j} & \underline{k} \\ 1 & 6 & -3 \\ 2 & 1 & 3 \end{vmatrix}\]
Kyun: Pehli row mein unit vectors \(\underline{i}, \underline{j}, \underline{k}\), doosri row mein pehle vector ke components \(\underline{a}\), teesri row mein doosre vector ke components \(\underline{b}\). Rows ki tarteeb wohi honi chahiye jo product ki tarteeb hai, warna jawab ka sign ulta ho jayega.

Teenon minors nikalein
\[\underline{i}\text{ minor} = (6)(3) - (-3)(1) = 21\]
\[\underline{j}\text{ minor} = (1)(3) - (-3)(2) = 9\]
\[\underline{k}\text{ minor} = (1)(1) - (6)(2) = -11\]
Kyun: Har unit vector ki row aur column ko dhak dein (cover kar dein); jo 2 by 2 bachta hai us ka (upar baayan)(neeche daayan) minus (upar daayan)(neeche baayan) minor hai. Har product ko bracket mein likhne se negative signs ki ghalti nahi hoti.

Signs \(+, -, +\) lagayein
\[\underline{a} \times \underline{b} = \underline{i}(21) - \underline{j}(9) + \underline{k}(-11)\]
\[= 21\underline{i} - 9\underline{j} - 11\underline{k}\]
Kyun: Determinant ko pehli row ke saath kholte waqt signs ka pattern \(+, -, +\) hota hai, yani beech wala \(\underline{j}\) ka term minus ho kar aata hai.
Dhyan dein: Sab se zyada ghalti isi beech wale minus mein hoti hai; \(-\underline{j}(\text{minor})\) mein minor khud negative ho to jawab plus ban jata hai.

\(\underline{a} \times \underline{b}\) ki lambai (magnitude)
\[|\underline{a} \times \underline{b}| = \sqrt{(21)^2 + (-9)^2 + (-11)^2}\]
\[= \sqrt{643}\]
Kyun: Kisi bhi vector \(x\underline{i} + y\underline{j} + z\underline{k}\) ki lambai \(\sqrt{x^2 + y^2 + z^2}\) hoti hai (3D mein Pythagoras). Negative components ka square bhi positive hota hai, is liye har term bracket mein square karein.

Plane par perpendicular unit vector
\[\hat{n} = \pm\dfrac{\underline{a} \times \underline{b}}{|\underline{a} \times \underline{b}|}\]
\[= \pm\dfrac{21\underline{i} - 9\underline{j} - 11\underline{k}}{\sqrt{643}}\]
Kyun: Kisi vector ko us ki apni lambai se divide karne se rukh (direction) wohi rehta hai lekin lambai 1 ho jati hai. Misaal: farsh par seedha khada khamba upar ki taraf bhi plane par perpendicular hai aur neeche ki taraf bhi; isi tarah do unit vectors bante hain, is liye \(\pm\) likha. Answer key sirf plus wala deti hai; sawal "a unit vector" maangta hai, to koi bhi ek kaafi hai, lekin dono jaanna behtar hai.

\(\underline{a}\) aur \(\underline{b}\) ki lambaiyan
\[|\underline{a}| = \sqrt{(1)^2 + (6)^2 + (-3)^2}\]
\[= \sqrt{46}\]
\[|\underline{b}| = \sqrt{(2)^2 + (1)^2 + (3)^2}\]
\[= \sqrt{14}\]
Kyun: \(\sin\theta\) ke formula ke denominator mein dono vectors ki lambaiyon ka product aata hai, is liye pehle yeh nikal lein.

Angle ka sine
\[\sin\theta = \dfrac{|\underline{a} \times \underline{b}|}{|\underline{a}|\,|\underline{b}|}\]
\[= \dfrac{\sqrt{643}}{\sqrt{46}\,\sqrt{14}}\]
\[= \dfrac{\sqrt{643}}{\sqrt{644}}\]
Kyun: Definition \(|\underline{a} \times \underline{b}| = |\underline{a}||\underline{b}|\sin\theta\) ke dono taraf \(|\underline{a}||\underline{b}|\) se divide kiya. Do vectors ka angle \(0\) se \(\pi\) (180 degree) tak hota hai, aur is range mein sine kabhi negative nahi hota, is liye \(\sin\theta\) ka sirf positive jawab hai.
Dhyan dein: Yahan \(\pm\) mat lagayein; \(\pm\) sirf unit vector ke saath tha.

Tasdeeq: \(\hat{n}\) waqai \(\underline{a}\) par perpendicular hai
\[\underline{a} \cdot (\underline{a} \times \underline{b}) = (1)(21) + (6)(-9) + (-3)(-11)\]
\[= 21 - 54 + 33 = 0\]
Kyun: Dot product zero aaya, yani 90 degree ka angle, is liye cross product sahi hai. Isi tarah \(\underline{b}\) ke saath bhi zero aata hai; khud kar ke dekhiye.
